[Interpretation] Whereas paragraph 28 says that a discussion on the new constitution, the so-called Christmas Constitution, warned the Serbian leaders: [In English] "The public discussion on the Croatian Constitution has already alerted Serbian leader to what were for them the document's problematic features cited about. On 21st December 1990, the day before its proclamation, the Provisional Presidency of the Community of Municipalities of Northern Dalmatia and Lika declared a Serbian Autonomous District (SAO) of Krajina and adopted a statute." [Interpretation] Right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see those paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm grateful for you for having established a wider context in this paragraph. So we can see that that was a synchronised course of events. And in the same paragraph, you say that the Serbs demanded territorial autonomy, and you say: [In English] "In other words, at this point, the Serbian leaders in Croatia were not claiming anything that the Belgrade leadership was not willing to concede in Serbia." [Interpretation] So you thought that what the Serbs were requesting in Croatia was not something that Serbia proper did not allow in its state?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where does it say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 28, the end of paragraph 28, where you say that the Serbs in Croatia called for territorial autonomy. In Article 6 of the 1990 Constitution, in the Constitution of the Republic of Serbia, it says that Vojvodina and Kosovo are also forms of territorial autonomy, and that what Serbs are demanding in Croatia is nothing out of the ordinary, and that it is nothing the Republic of Serbia proper would not have allowed to happen in its own territory; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the report points that out, yes. It was in the footnote, footnote 39.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, just to expedite things in future - I'm grateful to the witness for pointing that out - in posing questions and pointing to paragraphs in the report if, in fact, there's a reference to a footnote, then that would assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll do my best. Let's look at 1D3523, and let us see how the Constitutional Court of Yugoslavia evaluated the constitutionality of the Croatian Parliament act on the dissolution of Yugoslavia. This is a decision issued by the Constitutional Court of Yugoslavia. This was issued at the initiative of the Federal Executive Council, i.e., the Government of Yugoslavia and the Presidency of Yugoslavia. They instituted proceedings before the Constitutional Court on the assessment of the constitutionality of the resolution on accepting proceedings for the disassociation of the SFRY and the possible association of internal lands of sovereign republics, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a document that you highlighted as something that provoked Knin to react? Isn't that the document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, which document are you suggesting that was that prompted Knin to react to the decision or the -- or the resolution? The resolution, yes, the resolution, precisely, yes, prompted them to react.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, since this document will be admitted, let's first look at its third page, and let's see what the decision of the Constitutional Court was. That's the last page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Constitutional Court of Yugoslavia annuls the part of item 1 of the resolution on accepting proceedings for the disassociation of Yugoslavia, and so on and so forth. Are you familiar with this document and this decision of the Constitutional Court of Yugoslavia? Was it available to you at the time when you drafted your report?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Yes, I think I've seen this. I certainly can't remember the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at the composition of the Constitutional Court of Yugoslavia. The president of the Constitutional Court of Yugoslavia, Milovan Buzadzic, who is a Montenegrin; Judges Hrvoje Bacic, Croat; Slobodan Blagojevic, Serb; Krste Calovski, Macedonian; Omer Ibrahimagic, Muslim from Bosnia, and so on and so forth. Pjeter Kolja is Albanian; Dimce Kozarov, probably Macedonian; Ivan Kristan, Slovenian, and so on and so forth. Do you agree that was a representative composition of the Constitutional Court?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you seem to mean, by "representative," representative of the national structure of Yugoslavia. If the membership is as you described, it would certainly seem to be, and I think they strove for that, in fact. I don't know the backgrounds to the -- the political backgrounds of all these individuals or when they were appointed. I would comment that the many members of the Yugoslav League of Communists of whatever nationality were dedicated to the preservation of the Yugoslav Federation, as well as simply Serbs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can the document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If "the document" refers to those two or three pages, no objection.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1266, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The entire document is only three pages' long. I think it should be admitted as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, in late December 1990, the counter-intelligence of the JNA took a photo of Martin Spegelj, the minister of defence of the Republic of Croatia, when he was involved in the action of illegal arming of Croatian illegal troops, and he even gave them instructions to shoot JNA officers in the stomach in order to kill them. Do you remember that? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware of this incident. I believe it was in the press and so forth. But the details, I don't recall, and the exact circumstances of all this, I think it was a little bit contentious at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, you remember that there is no doubt that we can hear in the clip that members of the JNA had to be killed, as well as their wives and children, in their apartments by throwing bombs into apartments, by killing them in the street. I don't think that there is any doubt about that. Do you have any reason to doubt the authenticity of the video-clip that even aired on television?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I certainly can't remember all the words that were spoken or even remember all the images. I have a vague recollection of all that, and I also seem to recollect that there was some controversy about whether the tape was authentic, or staged, or what, all that sort of thing. It's not something that I looked into.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Spegelj, and later on Josip Boljkovac were secretly recorded saying that the Serbian issue in Croatia would be forcibly resolved. Spegelj even used the term that the Serbs in Croatia will be butchered, and Boljkovac used the word "forcibly." Do you know that that was happening and that all those developments created fear and terror among the Serb population?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really can't recall these particular statements by Spegelj and Boljkovac. But as far as I am aware, there was a great deal of apprehension among Serbs in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree -- and we are going back to Bosnia. Do you agree that the Party of Democratic Action, up to mid-January 1991, up to a time after the election, was in favour of preserving the Yugoslav Federation, that that was their position?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I recollect - I have a better recollection of that document - their programme in 1990 favoured preservation of the Yugoslav Federation in its present composition; that is, with all the republics remaining within the Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that the Presidency of Yugoslavia, on the 9th of January, 1991, reacted when they obtained evidence about the legal import of arms into Croatia and Slovenia, and that they issued a decision on the dissolution of all illegal armed forces?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recollect something like that. Again, the date is something that I couldn't confirm off-hand, but I'm sure that the transcript of that Presidency session and the text of any decisions they issued would be available.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report 12125, paragraph 31, you conclude correctly that the separatist attempts had put the SDS of BiH on its guard. That is in paragraph 31; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 30th of January, 1991, and you will find it in paragraph 30 of your document, there was a first attempt to adopt the declaration on the sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and you conclude that that proposal was hindered by the 20 SDS deputies, and instead of adopting it, they sent that proposal -- they referred it for consideration to the National Council?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, paragraph 30 deals with those issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 21st of February -- I'm reading from paragraph 29, which refers to that same thing. You again correctly conclude that: [In English] "Croatia took a further step toward loosening its ties with the federation on 21 February 1991 when the Sabor adopted a constitutional law on supplementing the constitutional law for the implementation of the Constitution of the Republic of Croatia ..." [Interpretation] And so on and so forth. I don't want to go on reading the entire paragraph. Is that, indeed, what happened, what you recorded in your report? Did the Serbs in Croatia suffer an additional blow from this and as a result of this?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I would say there was a further blow to the Serbian position in Croatia, the position of the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. To avoid wasting time, we would offer 29 decisions in a Bar Table motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that all these decisions of the Croatian Assembly were abolished by the Constitutional Court of Yugoslavia as unlawful and unconstitutional?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't recall each specific decision. But along the lines of the decision you just showed, I can well imagine that they took decisions in regard to these actions as well. I think there's a whole book or collection of these things; that is, the decisions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to draw everyone's attention to your paragraph 35 in this same document, where you say that the decisions of the Assembly on the dissolution of the SFRY, you say that the Executive Board of SAO Krajina reversed them and declared that laws of Croatia which were in conflict with federal provisions and the provisions of the SAO would henceforth not apply in SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that what your paragraph 35 says?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's generally what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At this same time on the 27th of February, 1991, in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Avdo Campara, and that's paragraph 34 -- it says that Avdo Campara, invoking Amendment 70 to the Constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina, once again prevented the enactment of the Declaration of Independence and sent it back before the Assembly. That was the second time the Serbian community, the Serbian side, tried to prevent the enactment of this resolution; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can see what the paragraph says, and that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see D256 briefly to see what was said at the same Assembly session by Mr. Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall Mr. Izetbegovic said at the same session that he would sacrifice peace for a sovereign Bosnia, and he would not sacrifice sovereign Bosnia for anything?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I certainly recall that, that remark by Mr. Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Page 101 in Serbian, and in English, page 4, but since you remember that, we don't have to call up the document. Do you agree that this statement by Izetbegovic should have found a place in your reports?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it certainly could have. I think I did mention the later remark that he made in March along the same lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It's not just you, but everyone who worked for the Prosecution included every joke I made, and this remark by Izetbegovic was not a joke; it was a very dangerous statement to make. But never mind. Do you remember that in Split, on the 30th of March, Izetbegovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Making comments -- and I'm sorry to rise, but if I don't, then it's an invitation for Dr. Karadzic to acknowledge the impropriety of making comments by saying, Never mind, and moving on, while, nevertheless, interjecting them. So I object to that practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, Dr. Karadzic, you will know the difference between a question and a comment. Confine yourself to pertinent questions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that on the 30th of March, 1991, at the same time, therefore, at a very well-known meeting of the presidents of the six republics in Split, said very publicly that the declaration on the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina would be adopted with or without the consent of Serbian deputies, although at that time the declaration was still before the council of national or international equality for their consideration?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the remark I was referring to earlier. I thought this was very important and indicative, since it ran directly counter to what seems to have been agreed at the Assembly session in February. I'm not aware that there ever was a council for national equality, in any case, but Izetbegovic's remark seems to ignore that procedure entirely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you aware of the fact that on the 31st of March, 1991, a decision was adopted to establish a military wing of the Party of Democratic Action, SDA, to be known as the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have not -- I can't recall having seen any documents to that effect. It may well be true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that on the 5th of May, 1991, during a visit to the town of Trogir, Tudjman said to the representatives of the Croatian Democratic Union that the people should be mobilised and at the ready?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have the same answer to that question, which would be that I can't recall having seen a document to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall that on the very next day, on the 6th of May, 1991, in Split, there occurred forcible protests against the JNA, and on that occasion one JNA soldier, Sasa Gersovski was killed, and several others were wounded, and there's a very well-known video footage of somebody strangling the young soldier in the turret of a tank? It's been shown many times.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I've heard of that. But, again, the date I couldn't testify to, I won't testify to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we then briefly see 65 ter 939. And for the parties, I can say it's mentioned in the pre-trial brief as well, paragraph 159. I mean, the document is mentioned in the pre-trial brief. Unfortunately, the Prosecution translated only the portion that was of interest to them, which I can understand, but in that case it says -- the title is "Vasil too shot at Sasa." Sasa is the Sasa Gersovski I just mentioned, a young soldier doing his compulsory service in the JNA. And the subheading says: "Through Spegelj's mouth, Croatia had long ago declared war to the JNA. The Kalashnikov that killed the soldier in Split was maybe held by a member of the MUP of Croatia, but at that moment Stipe Mesic, Janez Drnovsek and Bogic Bogicevic also had their hands on that rifle."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear Mr. Karadzic's question because we were still doing the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The question is: Were you given this document about this important and dramatic event by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it's in our collection, it would have been available to me. I can't recall having seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to show you, Dr. Treanor, that it matters much more to the Prosecution that a political organisation establishes some autonomous region than a dramatic event of this kind, such as the one in Split. Do you agree that it's a very dramatic event?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to be a dramatic event, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the entire document to be MFI'd, because only a portion has been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: So be it. That can be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1267, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On 12th May 1990, after these harrowing scenes in Split, a referendum was held in SAO Krajina about remaining within Yugoslavia, and you deal with it in your paragraph 43 of this same document; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's mentioned in paragraph 43.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have evidence that it was Milosevic who advised and recommended this referendum or is it the case that the referendum was organised without the knowledge or even contrary to the wishes of Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have any document that would indicate that Milosevic specifically recommended this particular referendum. The comment in the paragraph says "of the type advocated by Milosevic." He had, I think in at least one of the speeches that was quoted earlier, said that referendums should be held of the peoples to see their desires about remaining or leaving Yugoslavia, so this is the type of referendum that he was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On 19 May 1991, and that's in paragraph 44, a referendum was held in all of Croatia, and the proposition was that the Republic of Croatia be a sovereign and independent state that guarantees cultural autonomy and civil rights to Serbs and members of other nationalities in Croatia. Is that written in your paragraph 44?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just to the interests of time, questions asking a witness to confirm what's in front of us, there have been repeated admonitions about that, and it's certainly unnecessary when presented to the person who wrote it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes. Dr. Karadzic, stating the obvious is not using your time efficiently.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. But I would really like to make an introduction for the next document, 1D3538, where the Constitutional Court of Yugoslavia overturns this decision that turns the Serbian people in Croatia from a constituent people into a national minority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here, on page 1, it says that: "The Federal Executive Council instigated before the Constitutional Court ..." Do you agree that at that time, the president of the Federal Executive Council, that is, the federal prime minister, was Ante Markovic, a Croat?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then see the next page, where the decision is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The whole decision says that the peoples made a union, and that one republic cannot decide on their rights and relationships, and the decision says: "This decision of Croatia is hereby abolished." This is to be published in the Official Gazette, et cetera. You can see who was on this council -- sorry, the Constitutional Court. It's the same composition, and those judges were delegated by the republics, nobody elected them contrary to the will of the republics. Now, the question is: Dr. Treanor, did you have insight into this decision of the Constitutional Court abolishing the decision to which you referred in paragraph 44?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I think I indicated earlier, we have all these decisions available.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document be admitted, this decision of the Constitutional Court?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection to the decision, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Insofar as the referenced parts are concerned, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1268, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am tendering the whole document. It's just three pages, and that includes the statement of reasons for this decision of the Constitutional Court with all the arguments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, there has to be a limit, and the limitation is basically that part of the document which has been put to the witness and to which the witness can speak.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then we'll have to offer more documents through a Bar Table motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, please, Dr. Treanor, in paragraph 45 of your report, you confirm that SAO Krajina's status was proclaimed, and the independent autonomous region proclaimed it was staying in the federal state of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And I would observe, in this connection, that the description as an autonomous political territorial region within the FRY goes beyond the status that they had been claiming, as we discussed earlier in connection with paragraph 28 and footnote 39.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But can you see that in the meantime, there happened something that was reversed by the Constitutional Court, and that this was a reaction to the developments?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I hope we can all see that from what's in the report, although the Constitutional Court's decision is not mentioned, which -- what -- I didn't catch the date of that decision, but presumably it would have taken some time for that to happen, and this reaction took place rather quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On 25 June 1991, paragraph 54, you state that Slovenia and Croatia proclaimed their independence. Would you agree that these decisions were contrary to the Constitution of Yugoslavia? In fact, if you don't want to deal with legal issues: Do you know that the Constitutional Court reversed this decision as well?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can well imagine that would be the case.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We will offer that decision of the Constitutional Court, reversing the decision on the independence of Slovenia and Croatia, through a Bar Table motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You also state in paragraph 54 that the JNA took steps to protect the borders of the SFRY. Do you agree that this action on the part of the JNA was their constitutional duty?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've referenced particular documents there as a basis for my knowledge of those particular events. I -- again, whether it was their constitutional duty to do that, I couldn't comment on that beyond what may be stated in the document, itself, which I can't recall at this time by way of any sort of preamble or whatnot to what -- to those particular documents. These types of decisions normally included at the beginning references to the -- to their legal basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were aware of the course of events and the attempts of the Muslim and Serb communities to avoid this adverse course of events, and that they were in the process of making a so-called historic Serbian-Muslim agreement; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, there were negotiations going on, as indicated in the report, between SDS leaders and various Muslim political leaders; in particular, the leaders of the MBO, the Muslim Bosniak Organisation, as well as the SDA, headed by Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Along with that historic Serbian-Muslim agreement, you were aware, as I can see, that Serbs also came up with a document listing their proposals. Do you recall that in July, the same time when this agreement was on the table, the Serbs presented their proposals?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first let me say I don't think there ever was an agreement. There was a discussion about having an agreement, about coming to an agreement, and I think I did reference the -- both the Serbian, that is, the SDS proposals and the MBO proposals, as they were made at that time, as they were later published.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, we'll take a break now until 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Just before you recommence, Dr. Karadzic, I've been reminded that I did not state in open court what is, in fact, I suspect, blindingly obvious, that we are still sitting under Rule 15 bis, in the absence of Judge Kwon. We did so yesterday, and we will do so tomorrow. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to call up 1D0897 in e-court. This is a document known under the title: "What is it that the Serbs propose?"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that in July, when this proposal appeared, and throughout August, an agreement was -- between Serbs and Muslims had been tabled? It was not accepted, but there were negotiations about that agreement until the very end of August, when Izetbegovic finally decided to opt out of it. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this document. I believe it's mentioned in the report -- in the -- perhaps in the report, but certainly in the leadership study.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 48, you, indeed, mention this document. If I may draw your attention, as well as the attention of all the others, you mention, in the footnote, that this refers to what the Serbs propose, and in paragraph 48 you say: [In English] "There is no way, except brutal force, that the Serbian people in BH might be separated from Yugoslavia." [Interpretation] Do you agree that this quote suggests that the Serbs -- or, rather, that the Serbian leadership were in favour of the war option?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't say that necessarily suggests that. It may suggest that they were just in favour of remaining in Yugoslavia, and that it would be better to do so peacefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry. Just so the record is clear, Your Honour, with reference to paragraph 48, it's not the case that Mr. -- that Dr. Treanor said there is no way, but he quotes the SDS thesis on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's plain, but it needs to be on the record. Thank you, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. I did say that that was a quote, but that I did not agree with the selectivity that was applied, because the sentence out of the context may suggest that the Serbs were in favour of the war. And now can we look at page 6 in the Serbian and page 4 in the English version of the same document, paragraph 11. I will not read. I would kindly ask everybody to look at paragraph 11, where the Serbs declare their political position with regard to Yugoslavia and Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It arises from this paragraph that the Serbian people were in favour of a democratic resolution to the crisis, without any use of force and without any solutions being imposed on them. Do you agree that that was the position that was unambiguously highlighted in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the paragraph says what it says.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now go to pages 3 and 4 in Serbian and pages 1 and 2 in the English version of the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Towards the end of the Serbian page is that the main idea, as the starting point of the Serbian Democratic Party for Bosnia and Herzegovina, is that: "Primarily nobody has the right to impose any solutions on anybody. Every attempt to cancel the right of those people who want to live in a" - the following page in the Serbian, please, and in English as well - "common state of Yugoslavia is unjust and absurd. On the other hand, no one must be prevented from leaving Yugoslavia when such agreements as do not jeopardise the rights of other nations living on the same territory have been negotiated. If this is technically possible, the Serbian side accepts the right of every people either to stay," which was technically possible because that would have meant the status quo, "or to leave Yugoslavia." Now, Dr. Donia [as interpreted], may I ask you: Did those who were in favour of the status quo need to use force, or is it the fact that the force was needed by those who wanted to secede from Yugoslavia, in other words, they were not in favour of a status quo?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was the position of the SDS at this time, as we discussed a little bit yesterday in my testimony, that since Bosnia was in Yugoslavia, and the Serbs in Bosnia were in Yugoslavia, then all they had to do was just remain in Yugoslavia, maintain the status quo. And they thought that that would be very easy and that would certainly -- if that's what happened, that would maintain the peace, which I'm sure everyone wanted to do, unless they wanted to leave. Then they had to change the status quo. Then it becomes a question of how that gets done. You referred to force. What do you mean by "force"? I mean, the procedure that the SDA and the HDZ adopted at the session of the Assembly on the 14th and 15th of October, passing the resolutions they did, the so-called memorandum and letter, that that could broadly be described as using force.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that before the years of physical force, we called that constitutional violence? All the decisions that were taken in the Parliament imposing decisions on the other people, we called it the constitutional violence; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that particular term. I certainly remember things being said about the Constitution having been violated, the constitutional order having been destroyed, so it would seem that the SDS leaders did regard that as a form of violence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go back to the 12th of July, 1991, and the Assembly of the Serbian Democratic Party. And now I would like to draw your attention to paragraph 59, in which you write about the so-called Belgrade Initiative. We will go back to the 12th of July and the Assembly later on. This is what I said, and it was mis-recorded. And now I want to draw your attention to paragraph 59, in which you write about the so-called Belgrade initiative. The document number is 65 ter 6586. While we are waiting, let me ask you this: Do you remember that we, the Serbs, and the Serbian Democratic Party and the other Serbian party, gave up on regionalisation in favour of the Serb-Muslim agreement, and that was publicised? We gave up on SAOs and autonomous if we were able to reach an agreement between Muslims and Serbs which would result in the preservation of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not precisely aware of that, no. I know that regionalisation continued to -- or seemed to continue to figure in negotiations with Mr. Zulfikarpasic and Mr. Izetbegovic, and that Mr. Zulfikarpasic in August, as I think it may be referenced in the report, had a series of articles in the Sarajevo daily "Oslobodjenje," among other things, rejecting the idea of regionalisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll talk about regionalisation specifically. However, since I've mentioned the Belgrade Initiative, I wanted to ask you this: You mention it in paragraph 59. Let me ask you, do you agree that that meeting took place in August, and that there was a debate based on the historical Muslim and Serb agreement, that the initiative for this was the historical Serb-Muslim agreement that was being negotiated at the time?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to the paragraph, the -- and my information, the meeting took place on the 12th of August in Belgrade, and it was connected with the so-called historic agreement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can the previous document be admitted, the title "What do the Serbs propose?", as well as the document entitled "The Belgrade Initiative"?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes. The first document, I gather, is already in evidence. The second one can be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that was Exhibit D288 under 65 ter 942.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And has "The Belgrade Initiative" been given a number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is the document that we see on the screen the document that you referred to in your paragraph 59, sir?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it seems to be. I can't see the ERN, but it looks familiar.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Has the initiative been admitted, the one on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yeah, I think it has been.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, "The Belgrade Initiative" document will be Exhibit D1269.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We don't have much time to talk about the developments in Croatia in August. However, I would like to draw your attention to paragraph 61, in which you write about a meeting of the Presidency of Yugoslavia and other Yugoslav leaders. The meeting took place on the 21st and the 22nd August. I'm asking all the participants in the proceedings to look at paragraph 61. What I would like to know is this: Do you agree that you noted and highlighted here that the Serbian leaderships from Serbia and Montenegro proposed that the right of all the people to self-determination should be respected, that procedures by the Federal Assembly should be adopted for the separation of those republics who wished to do so, and that they shouldn't be imposing solutions on any of the peoples?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the paragraph says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the adoption of the laws on legal secession, a process that had been underway, was largely ignored by Croatia and Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the details of that process, but they certainly seemed to me to have adopted their resolutions without reference to any such process.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 65, you say that Borisav Jovic defined the role of the Yugoslav People's Army, and you say, amongst other things: [In English] "Our goal is using the institution of the JNA, as a legitimate military force of Yugoslavia, to force the Republic of Croatia to not realise its interests by force and to force the Republic of Croatia that it must accept the political search for a solution that will secure the right of the Serbian people to self-determination."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the paragraph says --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me. I didn't think -- I didn't hear a translation. I think that was the problem that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes, nor did I, so that wasn't translated, Dr. Karadzic. You may have to repeat yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Allow me to go on reading from the second paragraph: [In English] "It is not the aim of the JNA to topple Croatian authority and to impose some authority on the Croatian people, rather to make it impossible for Croatia to impose solutions by force on the Serbian people in Croatia. This means the goal is very clear. The JNA is for the purpose of the right of every people to self-determination, and in practice for the purpose of the right to protection of the Serbian people in Croatia."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question is this: Is this an obviously well-defined role of the JNA, to protect rights, and not to impose solutions on Croats?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the paragraph says what it says. I notice there is -- in the first line there, first and second line of the quote, we're having the JNA forcing people not to use force. It sort of gets into the chicken-and-egg argument you were referring to before. But the paragraph does say what you've indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, if the JNA had to or could prevent Croatia from using force, then everything would have fallen in its own place; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. That's kind of a counter-factual question. I don't know what would have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 7th September 1991, you say, in paragraph 72, efforts were launched by the European Union, headed by Lord Carrington, to find a solution; right? Do you agree that that agreement also applied to the outer borders of the federal state of the SFRY? To be more precise, let me quote: [In English] "We are determined never to recognise changes of any borders which have not been brought about by peaceful means and agreement." [Interpretation] That is a part of the declaration which was read at the ceremonial opening of the Conference on Yugoslavia. You mentioned that in your paragraph 72. Does this also apply to honouring the existing external or outer borders of the federal state of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's a very good question, and I don't know the answer to that off-hand. I'd have to go back and look at those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps notice that in the indictment, even the borders of the municipalities are codified even more than the external borders of Yugoslavia, as an internationally-recognised state? It seems that a lot more attention was paid to any changes made in the boundaries of the municipalities than to the borders of the former state of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: You make reference to the indictment. I don't really know what's in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 11th of September, do you agree that the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, at the proposal of Mr. Izetbegovic, passed a conclusion on not imposition of solutions for Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 11th of September? I don't recall that resolution. If you say so, I'll accept your word for it. I've read all the relevant documents, but I don't happen to recall that. But I think that that idea is expressed in the SDS Deputies Club meeting of the 30th of September that we saw yesterday. I think I may have mentioned that in my testimony, pointed it out. I think it's also mentioned in the report, that -- where Dr. Karadzic is quoted as saying in that meeting that Izetbegovic had agreed that force would -- that the will of one nation would not be imposed on another, and had agreed to discuss regionalisation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let's look at D265 very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Until then, Dr. Donia [as interpreted], let me remind you of the sequence of events. July and August, the Serbian-Muslim agreement is on the table. It was cancelled towards the end of August by Izetbegovic. In September, the Autonomous Region of Krajina was proclaimed. And then in the end of September, Izetbegovic accepted that no solutions would be imposed on Bosnia-Herzegovina. Now we are looking at the Official Gazette of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Can the conclusions be blown up also in English for the benefit of all the participants in the proceedings. It says here that there is a danger that war might spill over from Croatia to Bosnia, and so on and so forth. The Assembly is committed to finding a political solution. What is highlighted here is that all proposals should have an equal treatment, regionalisation, division into three republics, that all of them are equal, and that no solutions would be imposed on any of the peoples. Do you agree that that was a fact, and did you have access to these conclusions?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that seems to be what it says. I believe we have these documents. I would only point out that Mr. Izetbegovic was not a member of the Assembly. He was a member of the Presidency and was the head of the SDA, so his position -- the fact that he took the same position independently of this is also important, and which is what I discussed earlier. This is certainly a very interesting document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that already at that time, the Party of Democratic Action had a large number of regional military staffs of the Patriotic League, that in Sarajevo there was a staff of the Patriotic League, and there were also municipal staffs of the Patriotic League? By September, they existed in all of 90 municipalities, and later in 103 municipalities?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not really familiar with the details of their organisational structure or the extent of that structure.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then see D298. It's already in evidence. I want to just remind Dr. Treanor. D298, page 2 in English and Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, let me ask you: In your view, was it natural for the Serbian side to feel uneasy in a situation where the other side is setting up an illegal army?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, that's sort of a chicken-and-egg question, and I think it was not surprising that many people in -- not only in Bosnia-Herzegovina, but throughout Yugoslavia, felt uneasy at the development of events.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I ask you to look at paragraph 3: [In English] "Immediately after involving myself ..." [Interpretation] Well, let us note first this is a document from Sefer Halilovic, who later became commander of the Main Staff of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. But before he was appointed to that position, he secretly worked to establish the Patriotic League. As we can see, in September -- that's paragraph 1. In September 1991, he put all of his efforts into forming the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but then another paragraph says: "Immediately after involving myself in preparations ..." Please read that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm not quite clear what paragraph you're referring to. Maybe it would be better if you just read it. I don't think I've ever seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [In English] "Immediately after involving myself in preparations for the defence of RBH, in September 1991, together with the late Safet Hadzic, who was appointed president of the Crisis Staff of the Sarajevo region, and with the help of Mirsad Causevic, now in the MIP/Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Senad Masovic, now at the Command of the 3rd Corps, I drew up a proposal for organising the Patriotic League for the Sarajevo region and reorganised the regional staff of the Patriotic and the plan for the defence of the Sarajevo area."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That appears to be what it says. It does say "MIP," which is the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, rather than Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's correct. But now I'd like to remind you of paragraph 12, where the Serbs were accused, in the pre-trial brief, of negotiating, on the one hand, and preparing for conflict at the same time. Dr. Donia [as interpreted] -- no, Dr. Treanor, do you know of a single military organisation of the Serbs in September 1991?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the military structure and organisation among Serbs at that time, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 68, you state that Karadzic lost his faith in Izetbegovic on the 15th October: [In English] "Karadzic's faith in Izetbegovic was destroyed on the 15th of October, 1991. The 8th Joint Session of the SRBH Assembly, which was adopted on the 10th of October, and which convened for the second time ..." [Interpretation] The 14th of October. Please, everyone, look at this paragraph. That's the critical session of the Assembly where the Serbian deputies walked out. And after two abortive attempts in the spring of 1991, the resolution on the sovereignty of Bosnia-Herzegovina was finally adopted; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the paragraph says, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 65 ter 11311.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At that Assembly session, as you know, I made a speech that is often quoted, usually against me. Do you remember that speech?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page. The English page is 106. The Serbian page is 111. Because it's the whole transcript of that session, the numbering is different. Serbian, 111; 5English, 106.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that I said here: "I'm saying for the hundredth time, the Serbian Democratic Party is not creating the will of the Serbian people; it interprets it. We would be lying if we told you that you are able to vote for this and do something with it in Europe." Do you remember that the Serbian Democratic Party held the position that it was not pushing that programme; it was the Serbian people who wished it? Or let's move on with critical paragraphs. English page 108; Serbian page 111 -- sorry, 12. Bottom of the page in Serbian. It says: "We will thwart you, in the international and local public, in committing constitutional violence which is followed by all other types of violence. We don't control this situation anymore. It was said a hundred times from this -- from this pulpit this is the road to which you want to lead Bosnia and Herzegovina, the same path of suffering and hell that Slovenia and Croatia had already walked." Next page, please. The same speech before, explaining the proposal - whether I will explain it myself or leave it to someone else, I don't know - I have to clear up one thing that comes from the interpretation of what we say at this -- from this platform. That thing is related to the issue of war or peace. "For the 100th time, I have to repeat that Serbs do not threaten anyone with war. Serbs are only announcing that they will not be able to reach any decision reached by out-voting and to the detriment of others, and that Serbs could not be forced to live in the state in which they do not wish to live. Serbs and Muslims understand each other at least on that point, because Muslims are afraid that they would become a minority in the inferior, shrunk Yugoslavia, even though they enjoy the protection of their republic which will never become a constituent part of Serbia, but which will be completely equal with Serbia." So Serbs are afraid, by the same token, that in Bosnia and Herzegovina they could be out-voted on this occasion or after several years, it's completely the same. Would it not have been important for you to include the positions presented in this speech in your report?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said earlier, there were any number of things I could have included. The positions being taken here are perfectly consistent with the positions that have been taken for the previous year, some of which we discussed in testimony yesterday. I notice there seems to be an implication here, going back to our previous discussion, an implication that the Serbs would use force to prevent people from using force.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Donia [as interpreted] -- sorry, Mr. Treanor, that's not stated anywhere here. It says only that Serbs will not allow themselves to be forced to live in a state in which they do not wish to live. Serbs do not need to use force. We have every right, including constitutional rights, to live in the state in which we were living. Look at what it says further below. First of all, do you agree that force was not needed to stay in Yugoslavia; force was needed by those who wanted to secede?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I think we discussed this point before, that their position was that they were in Yugoslavia and they just wanted to stay in Yugoslavia. If the only way for that to change would be by force, I just meant referring to the previous document, where we saw the JNA forcing people not to use force. So if people are using force to make you do something, that was obviously one of the options that the JNA was pursuing, to prevent the use of force; that is, using force to prevent force.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us continue on the same page 116 in English. Karadzic says: "Please, gentlemen, Muslim leaders have clearly stated that if a catastrophe occurs, it would be, above all, a catastrophe for the Muslim people. It would also be a catastrophe for Serbian and Croatian people, especially the Serbian and Muslim people, since we are very mixed, while Serbs and Croats in Serbia are rather distanced, from a geographical point of view, except in the big cities, naturally. Dedijer presented information on the suffering of all the peoples in Bosnia and Herzegovina, especially Muslims, who could not be blamed for a mistake of one leader, or a small number of Ustashas among Chetniks or in Partisans, as Muslims were in all three parties. Decisions made by out-voting, decisions reached by majority nations, the chaos that could occur, the chaos that nobody will start, but has its own logic. The order is in somebody's hands, but chaos is not in anybody's hands. The basic feature of chaos is that nobody generates it, but it has its own logic and generates itself. Chaos could be caused by wrong intentions; above all, the intentions of the Muslim leadership to make something -- to do something for the Muslims that could be good for Muslims only, but it could not be good for Serbs at the same time. This could get us into chaos, which nobody could manage anymore. Let us understand each other well. The Serbian Democratic Party is not for chaos and, therefore, we are trying so persistently to make sure that no decision is made by out-voting others." On page 123 in Serbian, which is 117 in English, it says: "We can, therefore, send out a message that there will be no war." And above if, it says: "If we find a solution, if we manage to transform Bosnia by compromise ..." And the conclusion says: "We can send out a message that way, that there will be no war, no chaos, because order is in our hands, unlike chaos, which is in nobody's hands." Were you aware, Doctor, of this persistent advocacy and even begging and imploring of other sides to avoid descent into chaos?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm certainly aware that there were persistent agreements by the SDS leaders to -- at this time to negotiate to achieve their goal, which was to remain within Yugoslavia, which would have precluded -- hopefully, would have precluded chaos and so forth.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 130 in English and 137 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here, again, on behalf of the Serbian Democratic Party, I am enumerating what the Serbian Democratic Party had submitted to the Assembly: "In Bosnia-Herzegovina, there is no consensus among the three constituent peoples, Serbs, Muslims and Croats. There is no consensus on remaining in Yugoslavia or seceding from it. We may talk about the survival of the federal state of Yugoslavia, or about transforming it. However, there is no joint position on the issue. Serbs are in favour of the federal state, Croats were in favour of a confederation, and I don't know what they are advocating at this point. The Croatian Democratic Union was in favour of Bosnia-Herzegovina as an independent state, and probably the Party of Democratic Action will not express its wish for the independence of Bosnia at this moment. It is expressing its wish for change in the position of Bosnia related to the independence of Croatia, and that would make us also an independent republic against our will. "Position 2. However, there is the agreement in Parliament that the decision on the position of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Yugoslavia will be made democratically, with no use of force and without imposing the will of one group of people onto another. "Let me make the same comments. This is also the position of the Parliament" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speaker is kindly asked to read slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- "that there is no way that we impose --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Slow down a bit for the translators, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope the interpreters have this before them: "It's also the position of the Parliament that there is no way that we impose our will onto each other, because we have already made the Parliament conclusions that something like that will not be taking place. It means that we cannot achieve that by any kind of voting, I mean, imposing the will of one group of people onto another. Gentlemen, if we try to do that, then we will prove that we are not in favour of equality, that we do not comply with the decisions of the Parliament, that we do not comply with the Constitution of Bosnia and other documents."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Doctor, that this is advocacy for peace, not war?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is advocating reaching a decision by negotiation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 17th of October, two days after this Assembly session, the Serbian side, if you remember, sent an invitation to Muslims and Croats to reverse their decision on the sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina; otherwise, the Serbian side would proclaim the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina to include Serbian deputies to the Bosnian Parliament?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that particular document. I know there was a public proclamation made by the SDS at that time, which I think is referenced in my report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me ask you about the previous document, which is part of the transcript of an Assembly session -- Joint Assembly session. 65 ter 11311. Can this -- has this transcript, as such, been admitted, or should we tender just this speech? The Defence is not against admission of the entire transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, we have no objection either way, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll admit the entire transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1270, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see D295.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting: Do you agree, Dr. Treanor, that international conventions on human rights guarantee to us, as a constituent people, rights to self-determination, self-organisation, the use of our natural resources, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not familiar in detail with various international covenants. I know they exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at this demand to reverse unlawful decisions, and it says here that if this violation of our constitutional rights continues, we would form our own assembly. Do you recall this, or if you are seeing it for the first time, can you see that it was a public appeal made on the 17th of October?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be from a newspaper. I can't see all the headings. The translation date is the 25th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, right, on the 25th, after the establishment of the Assembly. But this is a reference to a news -- to a press conference that took place earlier. Do you agree that after the SDA and HDZ refused to reverse their unlawful decisions, on the 24th of October the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina was established, stating the following reasons? May this be received? Oh, it's been exhibited already. Can we see briefly P1343; page 7 in Serbian, page 9 in English. This is a statement of reasons for the establishment of the Serbian Assembly. The second paragraph in Krajisnik's contribution, it says: "In addition to all this, the present structure of the Parliament of Bosnia and Herzegovina does not include a constitutional and legal institution which would protect each of the three constituent peoples from being out-voted. True, in the essential rights of the national groups, an amendment to the Constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina of 1990 introduced the Council for National Equality, which was to decide on such issues by a consensus. However, this council has not been established to this day." So the president of the Constitutional Commission did not succeed in establishing this Council for National Equality, due to all sorts of obstruction. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall the speech, yes. I think we referred to that council before and the fact that it had not been established.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 8 in Serbian, page 10 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where Krajisnik says that not only the deputies to the Parliament, but also members of the Presidency from the Serbian Community were side-lined, marginalised. They are not informed about all sorts of activities that their president is taking. From the beginning, Serbian deputies were marginalised. That was done in order to keep them in the dark about all sorts of actions taken by the president of the Presidency. That continues on the next page in English. It says here on the same pages: "I believe that in this brief contribution, I pointed to the real reasons driving the Serbian Deputies Club when they decided to form the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina." These reasons, the stripping of legitimate Serbian representatives of their rights, did you include that in your report as the reasons why the Serbian Assembly was established in the first place?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this document is not quoted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Page 11 in Serbian, page 14 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you did state that the Serbian deputies and representatives in the government and the Presidency continued working in the joint bodies; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes. I believe I stated that, and I believe that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's see how Professor Najdanovic, Milutin Najdanovic, a well-known surgeon and an SDS party member, explained our position. This is in the third paragraph, where it says -- no, it is in the second paragraph in the Serbian language and also in the English language: "The Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina will consider and take decisions on issues related to the achieving of the equality of the Serbian people in relation to the other peoples and ethnic groups that reside in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and protecting the interests of the Serbian people, should those interests be compromised by the decision of the Parliament of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Serbian representatives will continue to work in the councils and working bodies of the Parliament of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina for which they were elected, until the ultimate solution to the crisis in Bosnia and Yugoslavia is reached. In the cases when we estimate that the acts of the parliamentary councils under consideration and adoption are compromising the equality of the national interest of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina shall work independently and take its own decisions." Do you agree that the Assembly of the Serbian People was actually a correction measure and a compensation for the non-functioning of the council of the peoples that we wanted to have, but that we never got?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the -- this assembly was similar to -- in that respect to the Serbian National Council that had been formed the year before; that is, as a body to express the will of the Serbian people and to seek to prevent any decisions being made against their will. By the way, I would point out that the institution of the Assembly is dealt with extensively in the original report, and not only in these paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 77 in your report, you list proposals by the Serbian representative in the Presidency of the SFRY, Mr. Boris Jovic. During the 154th session, he said that the key moment for them, as you say: [In English] "Whether they would continue to participate in the dirty business of the dissolution of the state ..." [Interpretation] And so on and so forth. And they said that they will continue to participate in the negotiations only if the concept was changed on the following basis: [In English] "For peoples who, by a referendum with international monitoring, wish to leave Yugoslavia. A constitutional/legal procedure of the Yugoslav Assembly should be secured to realise this with international monitoring." [Interpretation] And so on and so forth. I shall not go on reading the entire paragraph you wrote. Do you agree that the constituent people had the right to self-determination, according to all international laws that were in force?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about the international laws in force, but that, in general terms, peoples have a certain right to self-determination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your paragraph 76, you say that Jovic criticised Carrington's draft because he recognised the right to unilateral secession: [In English] "... which undermine the existing and internationally-recognised constitutional order of SFRY." [Interpretation] Do you agree that documents of unilateral secession were anti-constitutional and that they were also in violation of the international laws that were in force at that time?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, I couldn't offer an opinion on those legal and constitutional matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you aware of the Honourable Judge of this Tribunal Antonio Cassese's position on this matter? Can we now look at 1D1613.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You worked here until you were retired, until you were pensioned off, and he was the President of this Tribunal; right? Can we now look at --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is -- sorry, Your Honour. I rose to object to that. I thought Dr. Karadzic had moved on. The witness interjected an answer. I don't think we should be returned to it, and if we do, my objection stands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: The objection is a good one. Dr. Karadzic, this witness's views of the views of someone else, even someone as eminent as Professor Antonio Cassese, are not relevant to the workings of this trial.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency. However, I'm afraid that Dr. Treanor often proffers comments which imply that he accepts that unilateral secession is possible. Will you allow me to quote just one of Judge Cassese's sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, if you want, in due course, to make legal submissions and back it up with authorities, that's another matter. But for the moment, please simply cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Then we will stick to the historic overview that this witness is familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 9th of November, 1991 -- or, rather, on the 9th and 10th of November that year, a plebiscite of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina was organised, and you write about that in your paragraph 81. Do you agree -- you noted that. I suppose you do. Do you agree that nearly 100 per cent of the voters were in favour of staying in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know what the report on the results of the plebiscite said, and it -- that report stated the results as given in that paragraph 81.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you also agree that on the 11 December 1991, the Assembly of the Serbian People adopted the proposal of the recommendation on establishing the Serbian assemblies in the municipalities where decisions were being imposed on the Serbs through the process of over-voting, and that was only after that plebiscite was organised in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, I'm aware of that. Again, I think that event is mentioned in the original report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that there was also a need for the establishment of the Serbian assemblies in the municipalities, even where Serbs were minorities, but that there was no obligation to do so?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that's the view that was taken by the Bosnian Serb Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 19th December 1991, in your document 65 ter 952, paragraph 63, you talk about that 19 December, which was a very important day, and that was when the Main Board of the Serbian Democratic Party, in quotations "the Crisis Staff" -- the document number is 592, 65 ter 592. It is the first document, your first report. I thought I gave the correct number. Yes, that's the one. I'm talking about paragraph 63. Let me not read the entire paragraph. I invite everybody to look at it. And this refers to the document known as Variant A and B. It says here: [In English] "Alternatively, the party (SDS) rank in Serb minority areas would constitute new Serbian municipal institutions on parts of the municipal territories referred to as Variant B, thus dividing the existing municipalities and invariably setting the stage for conflict." [Interpretation] Thus, in your view, that was a plan for breaking up Bosnia and Herzegovina along ethnic lines and an instruction for illegal actions and taking territories. I will not go into establishing the fact whether the Crisis Staff, indeed, existed, and who drafted the document. I would rather ask you whether, in your analysis, you highlighted the other parts of those documents. For example, page 2 -- I apologise. I believe the document number is P5. P5; Serbian 2, English 1. P5; Serbian 2, English 1. English page 1, where it says: "Because there is reasonable ground for suspicion that certain forces are working persistently, thoroughly, and in an organised way to take Bosnia-Herzegovina, and hence also the Serbian people out of Yugoslavia by force, we hereby issue ..." And so on and so forth. Do you agree that taking Bosnia-Herzegovina out of Yugoslavia, which is referenced in this paragraph, is contrary to the will of the Serbian people, which also makes it a violation of the Constitution?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the paragraph you pointed to here sets out the reasons for the formulation of these instructions very well. I don't think, as we've discussed earlier, the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina, through the SDS - and there were SDS representatives in the Assembly, and I'll just remind the Court that almost all the Serbian deputies in the SRBH Assembly were part of the SDS party - wanted to stay in Yugoslavia. And you have referred earlier to constitutional violence in relation to attempts to take Bosnia out of Yugoslavia, against the will of those -- against the will of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina, so I think I can say that. Again, giving any legal or constitutional qualification to the action is something I would want to refrain from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The Serbian page can stay. Can we go to English 2. In paragraph 2, it says this was all done in order to enhance mobility and readiness to protect the interests of the Serbian people. Do you agree that the Serbian community was being motivated to prepare for defence?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think in general terms, yes, this document is --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It appeared to me the witness was in the middle of getting an answer out and was overridden, so I think he just needs an opportunity to complete it, if that's, indeed, what was happening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness complete his answers, please, Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I believe this is document is an effort to get the SDS ready to defend what they regarded as their territories.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise. I thought that the witness had finished. That's why I interrupted. I apologise. I am pressed by the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that Variant A speaks about the activities in the municipalities where Serbs constituted a majority, where Serbs were in power, and in that part a reference is made to taking power, but not taking over power from somebody?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, Variant A municipalities are the ones in which the Serbs constituted a majority. Almost invariably in that case, the SDS was in power in those municipalities. However, that does not mean that the SDS and its people even in those Variant A municipalities necessarily controlled all the important institutions in those municipalities. Dr. Karadzic, in his speech in connection with the upcoming plebiscite speech, which he gave on the 31st of October/the 1st of November, had enjoined SDS officials on the municipal level to consolidate their power and get hold of all the institutions that they were entitled to have control of in those municipalities. For instance, getting rid of directors of this, that, or the other enterprise who was not acting totally in conformity with their desires. In other words, just having gained the majority and gaining control of the Assembly and the high offices in the municipalities was not sufficient. It was necessary to actually make sure that reliable people were in every position, something which apparently had not happened by the end of October 1991. And I see this as a continuation of that effort in the Variant A municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A brief question now. Do you agree with me that the elections in 1990 led not only to changes in power, but also to changes in the system from the previous socialism to multi-party democracy, and that the Serbian Democratic Party kept a lot of, as it were, older politicians in their places because things just were not implemented as they should have been, as you say?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
