utterances.text: Well, I'm not -- yes, there certainly was a change of power that took place. Officials of the former League -- the League of Communists and its allies would have been in most of the positions in the -- on the municipal level. The extent to which they may all -- may not all have been replaced, I don't know. But what you are referring to here, I think, is the type of problem that I was referring to, that even though the SDS had won the elections in various places, they didn't necessarily control all the levers of power. And there was an effort, at the end of 1991, to make sure that this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you for introducing a new term, and that was to consolidate power, because in the indictment and the pre-trial brief, the term used is "taking over," whereas our term in Parliament is closer to your term "consolidation of power." Do you agree that this was not the case of take-over because there was nobody to take power over from, because we were already in power in those places? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Again, I'm sorry to rise. There's a question posed now which, of course, the witness can answer, but I object to comments and will continue to do so, and the accused should be admonished to refrain from doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, Dr. Karadzic, it's becoming a persistent habit. Apart from the fact that it's improper, you're acting as counsel and you must behave like counsel. A comment is not for counsel to make, but it also wastes your time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise. I just wanted to be efficient. I didn't want to go there, but it seems that we will have to deal with that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your paragraph 63, Dr. Treanor, you say that in that way, by the division of the existing municipalities into several municipalities [In English] "... is invariably setting the stage for conflict." [Interpretation] Do you believe that the division of Yugoslavia and unilateral secessions were not the case of setting stage for a conflict, and that the preservation of municipalities' boundaries was more important and more decisive than the preservation of the borders of an internationally-recognised state, the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. If I understand your question correctly, I think I would agree that the division of Yugoslavia in that the secession and attempted secession of various republics did set the stage for conflict.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at page 6 in Serbian and English, paragraph 8 in the A/B variant document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here: "Bear in mind that national and all the other rights of members of all the peoples are respected, as well as their subsequent engagement in the authorities that will be set up by the Serbian people in the municipality." Did you notice in your report that non-Serbs who lived in those municipalities were to be treated as equals and that they were to be given positions in the bodies of power?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that's mentioned in the report, no.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at page 9, both in Serbian and in English. And the paragraph I'm looking at is 6. I believe that we're now talking about Variant B. That is about the settlements in the municipalities where Serbs are a minority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where it says: "Organise secret observation posts and a system of communication to alert the Serbian population about any possible danger. In this regard, plan protection measures and resettlement of a population, moving personal effects to more secure and safer areas." Would you not agree that this is a very clearly-defined defence measure?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as -- in this passage here, that certainly seems to be what's being referenced, to defend Serbian areas. Talking about protection measures and resettlement of population, that's a bit ambiguous, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here: "Organise covert observation and a system of reporting all threats to the Serbian population." We have to bear in mind that this applies to the municipalities where Serbs are a minority. Does this not refer to protective measures that have been put in place in case of attack from other sides?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, it seems to be in that context, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And can we now look at page 10 in English, and page 9 can stay. Chapter III, paragraph 1. Roman III, paragraph 1, page 10 in English. Very well. "In order to carry out as effectively as possible its tasks, measures, and other activities defined herein, and also other tasks, measures and activities judged to be useful for the organisation of the Serbian people for its best possible defence and protection, the Crisis Staff must first undertake a comprehensive assessment ...," and so on and so forth. Is it clear and equally unambiguous that the reference which is made here is a reference to defence measures?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that seems to be being discussed, as we said at the beginning of this argument -- this discussion, sorry. I described this document as being one to get people organised and prepared to -- and defend the territories that they regarded as belonging to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, we're going to finish for today, and we will reassemble at 9.00 a.m. tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 3rd day of June, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.30 p.m.,
